newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO negotiator resigns over disputes with Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO negotiator resigns over disputes with Israel.

text.p: Top PLO negotiator Mahmoud Abbas has resigned from heading peace talks with Israel amid disputes with the Jewish state which threatened to delay a handover of West Bank land to the PLO, an aide said on Monday.
Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, handed Palestinian President Yasser Arafat his resignation letter after an unsuccessful meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy late on Sunday.
"Abu Mazen's resignation letter has been placed on the table of President Arafat," said Arafat's aide Ahmed Tibi.
"Abu Mazen is tired of these one-sided Israeli decisions -- the settlement at Har Homa, the closing of offices and the recent redeployment decision," he told Israel's army radio.
The radio said Arafat had not decided whether to accept the resignation. Abbas, among the main architects of the landmark 1993 Israel-PLO peace accord, could not immediately be reached for comment.

Israel angered Palestinians last week with its decision to hand over nine percent of the West Bank in the first of three withdrawals outlined in a 1995 peace agreement and reaffirmed in a deal in January between Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Palestinians say they were expecting 30 percent of the land.

The decision came on the heels of two other Israeli moves which irked Palestinians -- the approval to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem and the decision to shut down four PLO offices in East Jerusalem.
An Israeli official said on Wednesday Israel would not go ahead with the pullback after Abbas gave Levy a written rejection of Israel's plan.
"We have to give the area to somebody...It's up to them," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters after Levy met Abbas.
Israel says a U.S. note attached to the January deal left the extent of the pullback to its sole discretion. Abbas said Israel could not set the scope of the withdrawal unilaterally.
He also demanded that Israel freeze plans to build the 6,500 homes of Jews in East Jerusalem.
Palestinians regard the construction project as prejudicing negotiations on the city in final peace talks scheduled to start on March 17.
Levy said he made clear that Israel would not reconsider the construction project nor negotiate the West Bank withdrawal.
"The government of Israel is operating according to the agreement," he told reporters after the two-hour meeting.
Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the talks were in crisis and Ahmed Abdel Rahman, the general-secretary of Arafat's cabinet, suggested Palestinians might respond with violence.
"From now on, resisting settlements will not be through words, condemnation or complaints to the U.N. Security Council," he said in a speech on Sunday in Gaza.
Levy cancelled a trip to the United States in order to maintain contacts with the Palestinians.
